newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia to waive immunity of its diplomat in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Georgia to waive immunity of its diplomat in U.S..

text.p: Georgian leader Eduard Shevardnadze said on Friday he was prepared to waive the diplomatic immunity of a Georgian diplomat involved in a five-car crash in which a teenage girl was killed.

A written statment by Shevardnadze also said the diplomat, Georgy Makharadze, should stay in the United States until an investigation into the accident was completed "unless a different agreement between the two governments is reached".
The statement, which expressed Shevardnadze's concern over the accident, said: "The president of Georgia is prepared to waive the diplomatic immunity of Georgy Makharadze.
"Makharadze shall remain in the United States of America until the completion of the investigation and legal procedures unless a different agreement between the two governments is reached."
The statement appeared to be a response to a request by the U.S. State Department which on Thursday formally asked Georgia to waive Makharadze's immunity.
A car driven by Makharadze, 35, started a five-vehicle collision in Washington last Friday in which a 16-year-old American girl, Joviane Waltrick, died.
